strings.name: Ma Yansong
strings.role: Architect · Founding partner of MAD Architects
strings.summary: Ma's Shanshui City explores nature, emotion and the modern city. After founding MAD, he worked with partners and teams to move from conceptual experiments to towers, opera houses and museums, often using fluid forms to reshape architecture's boundary with landscape. Rotterdam's Fenix opened in 2025 and the Lucas Museum in Los Angeles in 2026. He also serves as Domus's 2026 guest editor.
strings.coverageNote: Selected verifiable milestones through 16 November 2026; not a live news archive.
strings.influence.rationale: Connects natural imagery and urban space through MAD, advancing Chinese architects' participation in international cultural buildings and towers.
strings.facts.f1.label: Birthplace
strings.facts.f2.label: Education
strings.facts.f2.value: Architecture bachelor's from Beijing University of Civil Engineering and Architecture; Yale MArch in 2002.
strings.highlights.h1.title: Translating landscape into buildings
strings.highlights.h1.text: Shanshui City brings the spatial imagination of Chinese landscape painting and gardens into contemporary urban design.
strings.highlights.h2.title: International cultural projects
strings.highlights.h2.text: Fenix and the Lucas Museum incorporate migration, visual storytelling and public space into architectural experience.
strings.timeline.t1.title: Lucas Museum opened
strings.timeline.t1.text: The Los Angeles museum, designed by MAD with Stantec, welcomed the public; Ma joined the opening program.
strings.timeline.t2.title: Named an AIA honorary fellow
strings.timeline.t2.text: The American Institute of Architects announced the designation recognizing his international practice.
strings.timeline.t3.title: Fenix and Rotterdam exhibition opened
strings.timeline.t3.text: The migration museum and its rooftop Tornado opened alongside a Nieuwe Instituut exhibition of MAD's work.
strings.timeline.t4.title: Harbin Opera House completed
strings.timeline.t4.text: Continuous surfaces and topography shaped a public cultural building within wetlands.
strings.timeline.t5.title: Absolute Towers completed in Canada
strings.timeline.t5.text: Two twisting residential towers broadened high-rise form and international discussion of MAD.
strings.timeline.t6.title: Ordos Museum completed
strings.timeline.t6.text: A curved metal volume responded to its new-city setting, becoming an early public landmark for the practice.
strings.timeline.t7.title: Founded MAD Architects
strings.timeline.t7.text: Returned to Beijing to establish the office, developing it with Dang Qun and Yosuke Hayano.
strings.timeline.t8.title: Completed Yale's architecture master's
strings.timeline.t8.text: Continued his Chinese education overseas and developed experience in New York and London offices.
